message:
feat(directory, keepalive-r2 (a)): standby relay leases -- one host-facing socket each, beside the legacy lease

Codex codex_keepalive_r2_spike_r1.md decision 1 (a). Local only: nothing is deployed, the NAS server is unchanged.

/api/connect {standby: true} (additive; default off = today's path) reserves the connect its OWN host-facing UDP
socket at mint time. A StandbyHello (104 B) with that capability binds the reservation to its client endpoint;
the lease then carries everything both ways through that socket: reserved -> provisional -> ready (host StandbyAck
Ok) -> active (HelloAck + DirectoryAuth after a StandbyActivate over the same lease). Several standby leases coexist
on one host; none drops another, and the legacy lease (observe socket, newest wins) neither drops them nor is
changed by them. A standby capability opens no legacy Hello, a legacy one no standby lease.

NAT path with no host change: the heartbeat lists one extra pendingPunch entry per reservation, aimed at
RELAY_HOST_FACING_IP:<its port> under a token no client holds (never the client's token twice -- a second listing
would let one capability admit twice). The host already punches every entry from its media socket; the reserved
socket pins the first datagram from the host's address (any port), takes nothing else, and a heartbeat does not
write its own tuple over a pinned lease (a host move releases the pin). Bounds: 8 per host with the legacy lease
counted, per account / per client wire IP / global sockets (env-overridable); a refused or failed reservation means
no relay candidate for that connect and `standbyRelay: <why>`. Everything is freed with the session (drop, sweep:
reservation TTL = capability TTL, provisional 30 s, client silence 60 s, closeHostsNow).

test/relay_standby_test.js (fake host behind a symmetric NAT, fake clients): 24 checks; run.js runs it (suite 791
PASS rc 0). Mutants: R1 standby via the observe socket, R2 legacy bind drops standby leases, R3 heartbeat overwrites
a pinned lease, R4 pinned lease takes any source, R6 legacy lease not counted -> each FAIL; R5 (standby token in a
legacy Hello) survives: the newest-legacy-token rule already refuses it.

Product / test / docs: product (directory server relay) / test (relay_standby_test, run.js) / docs (none).
